topic: For original equal-allocation pair-switching rerandomization on bounded finite-population triangular arrays, with fixed covariate dimension, fixed positive Mahalanobis threshold, finite Metropolis tuning, and nondegenerate outcome residual variance, derive the joint allocation-chain functional limit and its first-entry stopping law without assuming Markovian projected scores, stabilization, or outcome-residual independence. Prove that terminal standardized covariate imbalance is a radially clipped Gaussian, independent of a stationary Gaussian outcome-residual component, and that fixed tuning affects the proposal-time search clock but not the first-order terminal law. Establish stopped-design consistency of observed-arm projection moments and construct a computable variance-envelope critical value yielding sequencewise asymptotically conservative finite-population ATE intervals under heterogeneous effects; also derive the fully interacted adjusted corollary. Do not replace the original first-entry algorithm by its stationary or rejection-corrected variants, and do not claim shrinking thresholds, growing dimension, unequal arms, or finite-sample exactness. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An all-pairs coupling keeps the search path o_p(1) in arm empirical averages from a stationary uniform shadow over n-scaled horizons, and an exact antisymmetric-score identity cancels the Metropolis acceptance kink without assuming an empirical-law limit; exact absorption and cube-generator checks support the predicted drift, diffusion, radial entrance, and the necessity of variance-envelope critical values. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove trajectory-uniform predictable-characteristic bounds and assemble joint functional convergence, opposite-pair proposal-clock conversion, compact containment, martingale-problem uniqueness, and continuous first-hit transfer for the generally non-Markov projected scores. EARLY KILL TEST: Prove the localized actual-filtration characteristic lemma at a=1 for gamma=1 and 10 while stress-testing the six-row zero-correlation witness; pivot if an order-one residual term survives or any extra empirical-distribution or initialization assumption is needed. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_psrr_entrance_diffusion_ate.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the joint functional limit and first-entry terminal law of original equal-allocation PSRR at a fixed Mahalanobis threshold, including whether terminal imbalance is a radially clipped Gaussian independent of the Gaussian outcome-residual component.

source_refs.claim: The authors state that PSRR assignments are nonuniform on the acceptable set and leave asymptotic distributions of common statistics as future work.
source_refs.author: Ke Zhu and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: This work analyzes a stationary pair-switching chain and adds a rejection correction, rather than deriving the first-entry law of original PSRR.
source_refs.author: Jiuyao Lu, Tianruo Zhang, and Ke Zhu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhu and Liu explicitly leave the asymptotic distribution open, while the closest later work changes the stochastic object by moving to stationarity and adding a correction. For original PSRR, the allocation chain is Markov but its low-dimensional covariate and residual projections generally are not. First-entry transfer therefore requires trajectory-uniform predictable-characteristic bounds in the actual filtration, compact containment, martingale-problem uniqueness, and continuity of hitting the Mahalanobis ball; zero asymptotic covariance must yield Gaussian independence rather than being replaced by a residual-independence assumption.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint path-space weak-convergence theorem for standardized covariate and outcome-residual scores, with a continuous-first-entry result identifying the stopped covariate score as an explicit radial-clipping functional and the residual score as an independent stationary Gaussian component.

writing_exemplar.why: It defines the exact algorithm and isolates the missing asymptotic-distribution problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Classical rerandomization is statistically understood but computationally costly -> pair switching finds acceptable balance without uniform terminal assignments -> original stopped PSRR needs its own process and first-entry law

method_exemplars.technique: Control local drift and quadratic variation and identify a Metropolis diffusion through martingale-problem convergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the canonical process-level proof architecture, although PSRR additionally requires finite-population exchange characteristics and first-entry stopping.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply multivariate finite-population combinatorial CLTs after verifying maximal-term regularity for triangular arrays.
method_exemplars.why_closest: PSRR begins from complete randomization, making its joint Gaussian initialization and covariate-residual covariance finite-population vector-CLT objects.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether finite Metropolis tuning in original PSRR changes only the proposal-time search clock while leaving the first-order stopped allocation and terminal covariate-imbalance law invariant.

source_refs.claim: The tuning parameter controls acceptance of balance-worsening switches; robustness across tuning values is reported by simulation rather than proved as a limiting invariance.
source_refs.author: Ke Zhu and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: For a stationary pair-switching chain, invariant mass depends on tuning and uniformity is restored only by changing the algorithm with a rejection correction.
source_refs.author: Jiuyao Lu, Tianruo Zhang, and Ke Zhu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Simulation robustness does not distinguish invariance of the stopped state from a deterministic rescaling of search time. Stationary theory retains tuning in its invariant law but concerns a different long-run or rejection-corrected procedure. For the original first-entry chain, the acceptance kink must cancel in the actual-filtration score drift; otherwise an order-one tuning-dependent radial term can survive. The located literature does not derive the opposite-pair proposal-clock conversion on bounded finite-population arrays.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint limit theorem for the accepted-switch and proposal clocks that gives an explicit tuning-dependent deterministic time change while proving that the stopped score functional and radial entrance distribution are tuning-invariant.

writing_exemplar.why: Its algorithmic presentation treats tuning as a practical speed parameter and motivates separating computation from terminal-design behavior.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PSRR permits uphill switches to avoid local traps -> tuning changes how proposals become moves -> distinguish its computational search clock from the law of the first acceptable allocation

method_exemplars.technique: Extract an algorithm-speed constant from Metropolis acceptance probabilities while identifying the state diffusion after time rescaling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired PSRR theorem likewise separates a tuning-dependent clock from an otherwise invariant limiting stopped functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Write the pair-switching transition kernel explicitly, verify detailed balance, and isolate tuning dependence in proposal and corrective acceptance stages.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its kernel algebra is the nearest template for locating tuning, although the destination proof must stop before stationarity and cannot use the correction.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a computable variance-envelope critical value that yields sequencewise asymptotically conservative finite-population ATE inference under heterogeneous effects for original first-entry PSRR.

source_refs.claim: PSRR has exact Fisher inference under sharp nulls, but the general asymptotic distribution needed for heterogeneous-effect ATE inference is left open.
source_refs.author: Ke Zhu and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: Uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization has a Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian ATE limit and large-sample intervals without assuming additive effects.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding, and Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: Weak-null validity under rerandomization must account for the balance criterion because ordinary studentization can fail.
source_refs.author: Peter L. Cohen and Colin B. Fogarty
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.excerpt: precommitted independent-design conservative Wald result from this sequential adaptive same-path pivotal theorem

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature supplies valid inference for uniform acceptable-set rerandomization and exposes failures of naive weak-null studentization, while the prior reviewer explicitly separates precommitted independent-design Wald arguments from sequential same-path inference. Original PSRR is path-selected and nonuniform, so its clipped-Gaussian component cannot inherit the classical truncated-Gaussian reference law. Treatment-effect heterogeneity also leaves a finite-population covariance unidentified. A new argument must combine the stopped-filtration joint limit with optimization over covariance couplings compatible with observed-arm moments; otherwise sequencewise conservativeness is not established.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit stopped-PSRR limit law for the difference-in-means ATE estimator, a computable worst-case covariance-envelope quantile, and a theorem proving sequencewise asymptotic coverage of at least 1-alpha.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the closest motivation arc from design-induced non-Gaussianity to usable finite-population ATE intervals.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Balance-constrained assignment improves precision -> conditioning changes the ATE limit away from Gaussian -> derive the correct design-specific reference law and confidence interval

method_exemplars.technique: Orthogonally decompose the outcome contrast into covariate-projection and residual components, then derive quantiles of the resulting constrained-Gaussian convolution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: PSRR has the same finite-population projection geometry, with radial clipping replacing uniform Gaussian truncation.

method_exemplars.technique: Push a conservative estimable Gaussian covariance measure through a design-specific balance functional and prove stochastic dominance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed variance envelope is likewise a computable push-forward over covariance matrices compatible with observed finite-population information.

method_exemplars.technique: Use armwise residual-variance estimators to construct an estimated design-specific limit distribution whose quantiles conservatively dominate the true limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest established conservativeness argument for rerandomized ATE intervals under heterogeneous effects.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish stopped-design consistency of treated- and control-arm projection coefficients, residual variances, and covariate cross-moments under first-entry PSRR on bounded triangular arrays.

source_refs.claim: The defining PSRR theory does not establish stopped-sample moment consistency for its nonuniform terminal assignments.
source_refs.author: Ke Zhu and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: Regression-adjusted rerandomization inference relies on finite-population projection quantities and consistent armwise variance estimates under uniform constrained assignment.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: At first entry, arm membership is selected through the entire covariate-driven search path, so complete-randomization laws of large numbers cannot simply be conditioned on acceptance. The first proof step needed to transport regression-adjustment theory is uniform control of arm empirical averages over the random order-n search horizon, without adding an empirical-law limit, stabilization, or outcome-residual independence. The scanned literature contains no stopped-design uniform law for original PSRR.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A trajectory-uniform finite-population law of large numbers showing that every observed-arm projection and variance input used by unadjusted and interacted ATE procedures converges in probability at the PSRR stopping time to its finite-population target.

writing_exemplar.why: It explains why design-stage balance must be paired with analysis-stage estimability of projection and variance quantities.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Rerandomization changes sampling precision -> regression adjustment requires observable armwise projection quantities -> valid stopped-PSRR inference requires those quantities to remain consistent after adaptive search

method_exemplars.technique: Treat products and quadratic residual terms as vector finite-population outcomes and apply maximal-term CLT and law-of-large-numbers controls.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The needed projection moments are finite collections of assignment-weighted array statistics; PSRR adds uniformity over the stopped search path.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove consistency of treatment-specific OLS slopes and robust variance formulas under randomization without assuming the working linear model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the observed-arm quantities PSRR must recover before fully interacted design-based inference can proceed.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the design-based limit and robust-variance validity of the fully interacted regression-adjusted ATE estimator under original first-entry PSRR, including whether adjustment removes the radial-clipping component without outcome-residual independence.

source_refs.claim: Under classical Mahalanobis rerandomization, regression adjustment has design-based limit laws and conservative robust inference under heterogeneous effects.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: For rerandomization based on balance-test p-values, the fully interacted estimator is asymptotically efficient and its limit is unaffected by rerandomization.
source_refs.author: Anqi Zhao and Peng Ding

source_refs.claim: The original PSRR paper does not give asymptotic theory for regression-adjusted ATE estimators under first-entry terminal assignment.
source_refs.author: Ke Zhu and Hanzhong Liu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cancellation by full interactions has been proved for uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization and p-value-defined constrained designs, not for a nonuniform allocation selected at a path-dependent first-entry time. Under PSRR, the proof requires a joint stopped limit for covariate scores, outcome-residual scores, and estimated armwise slopes. Gaussian independence must be derived from the joint covariance structure and cannot be assumed at the unit-array level.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-population limit theorem showing that the fully interacted estimator has an explicit Gaussian residual limit under stopped PSRR, together with conservative domination or consistency of its robust variance estimator and an asymptotically conservative confidence interval.

writing_exemplar.why: Its design-versus-analysis framing is the natural template for presenting a PSRR regression-adjustment corollary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Design-stage balance improves unadjusted precision -> analysis-stage interactions remove linear imbalance -> determine whether cancellation and robust inference survive first-entry PSRR

method_exemplars.technique: Use separate treatment-arm linearizations for fully interacted OLS and prove robust-variance validity under finite-population randomization and heterogeneous effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination estimator is the same interacted regression functional, while the terminal assignment and moment-consistency argument must be replaced.

method_exemplars.technique: Project potential outcomes on design covariates, isolate the constrained imbalance component, and compare estimated and true asymptotic distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest complete design-based proof that regression adjustment cancels a rerandomization component while retaining conservative inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive joint regression-estimator limits under multiple balance regions and prove that full interactions make the sampling limit invariant to those constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It establishes the same cancellation phenomenon for other constrained designs, making first-entry PSRR the precise unoccupied setting.

literature_map:
Morgan and Rubin (2012, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/12-AOS1008) define classical Mahalanobis rerandomization as uniform rejection sampling over acceptable allocations.
Li, Ding, and Rubin (2018, PNAS, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1808191115) derive its finite-population Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian ATE limit and large-sample intervals.
Zhu and Liu (2023, Biometrics, DOI 10.1111/biom.13712; arXiv:2103.13051) introduce original first-entry PSRR and explicitly leave general asymptotic distributions open.
Lu, Zhang, and Zhu (2026, arXiv:2602.07613) analyze a stationary pair-switching chain and add rejection or resampling to restore uniformity, sharpening the distinction from original PSRR.
Krieger, Azriel, and Kapelner (2019, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asz026; arXiv:1612.02315) study greedy pair switching, whose nearly deterministic terminal design is not the PSRR Metropolis first-entry law.
Roberts, Gelman, and Gilks (1997, Annals of Applied Probability, DOI 10.1214/aoap/1034625254) provide the closest Metropolis diffusion-limit architecture, but not for finite-population pair exchanges or threshold stopping.
Li and Ding (2017, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2017.1295865) provide vector finite-population CLTs for Gaussian initialization and joint covariate-outcome scores.
Li and Ding (2020, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12353; arXiv:1906.11291) develop regression adjustment and conservative inference for uniform Mahalanobis rerandomization.
Lin (2013, Annals of Applied Statistics, DOI 10.1214/12-AOAS583; arXiv:1208.2301) is the core fully interacted regression and robust-variance exemplar under complete randomization.
Zhao and Ding (2024, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2024.105724; arXiv:2112.10545) show full interactions remove rerandomization effects for p-value balance regions, but do not analyze path-selected PSRR.
Cohen and Fogarty (2022, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12439; arXiv:2002.06654) show why weak-null rerandomization inference can require a design-specific Gaussian push-forward rather than ordinary studentization.
Wang and Li (2022, Annals of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/22-AOS2235) treat shrinking thresholds and diverging dimension, outside the fixed-threshold, fixed-dimension target.
Wang and Li (2025, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106049; arXiv:2312.02513) analyze best-choice rerandomization, whose selection law differs from first entry.
Zhou, Ernst, Morgan, Rubin, and Zhang (2018, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asy031; arXiv:1706.04182) analyze sequential-enrollment rerandomization rather than the all-at-once PSRR allocation chain.
The live tension is between inference for uniform constrained designs and computational pair-switching procedures whose original stopped output is nonuniform; no located paper supplies the joint PSRR path limit, tuning-clock separation, or stopped-design variance envelope.
